articles.title: Bethell's Unbeaten 76 Sinks India at Old Trafford. Bishnoi's 29-Run Over Hands England a 1-0 Series Lead.
articles.excerpt: Arshdeep took two wickets in the first over. Bethell took the match in the 17th. India trail in the five-match T20I series after a four-wicket loss in Manchester.
articles.image_caption: Emirates Old Trafford Cricket Ground in Manchester, venue for the second T20I between England and India
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of NRI fans packed Old Trafford, and millions more watched from the US, Canada, and UK — the T20I series offers the best live cricket viewing opportunity of the British summer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ounahi Scores Twice. Morocco End Canada's World Cup on the Fourth of July.
articles.excerpt: Canada were the better team for 45 minutes. Morocco were the better team for the match. A 3-0 loss in Houston ends the co-hosts' best-ever run.
articles.image_caption: Azzedine Ounahi of Morocco during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
articles.nri_angle: Nearly 1.8 million Canadians of Indian origin rallied behind the co-host side — the World Cup gave NRIs in Canada a source of unexpected civic pride, and the run inspired first-time football fans from Brampton to Surrey.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He's 15 Years and 99 Days Old. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Just Broke Sachin Tendulkar's 36-Year Record.
articles.excerpt: The Rajasthan Royals prodigy received his India cap at Old Trafford on Saturday, becoming the youngest male cricketer to represent the country — and ending a debate that began the moment he hit 72 sixes in IPL 2026.
articles.image_caption: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, India's youngest-ever international cricketer, photographed during a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi
articles.nri_angle: A generational shift in Indian cricket that NRIs across the US, UK, and Canada are watching unfold — the 15-year-old prodigy who broke Sachin's 36-year record represents the IPL era's first truly global cricketing sensation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fireworks, Then Football. The World Cup Takes Over the Fourth of July — and NRIs Have the Best Seats in the House.
articles.excerpt: Canada face Morocco in Houston at 1 PM ET. France meet Paraguay in Philadelphia at 5 PM ET. For Indian Americans, a holiday spent watching the world's biggest tournament on American soil is an experience without precedent.
articles.image_caption: The FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 16 bracket, confirmed after the final Round of 32 matches on July 3
articles.nri_angle: For 4.5 million Indian Americans, the Fourth of July has a new main event — two World Cup knockout matches on American soil, in cities with massive South Asian communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Salah Chipped a Panenka. Two Australians Missed. Egypt Made History in Dallas.
articles.excerpt: Mohamed Salah fought through a hamstring strain, scored the nerviest penalty of the shootout, and led Egypt to their first-ever World Cup knockout win — a 4-2 shootout victory over Australia in front of 70,244 fans at AT&T Stadium.
articles.image_caption: Mohamed Salah in action for Egypt's national football team
articles.nri_angle: The match was played at AT&T Stadium in the DFW metroplex — home to one of America's largest NRI communities — while NRIs in Australia saw the Socceroos eliminated from the World Cup.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kohli Is Back. Rohit Is Back. Bumrah Is Back. Gill Will Lead India Into England — and Toward the 2027 World Cup.
articles.excerpt: BCCI announces 15-member ODI squad for three-match series starting July 14 at Edgbaston. Kohli's fitness remains subject to clearance. England name Jofra Archer and uncapped James Coles in their own 16-member squad.
articles.image_caption: Shubman Gill, named captain for India's ODI series in England

sources.label: Wikipedia - Indian cricket team in England in 2026

articles.nri_angle: The three-match ODI series in Birmingham, Cardiff, and Lord's is the marquee cricket event for NRIs in the UK this summer, with India's biggest stars returning for a World Cup rehearsal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ronaldo vs Yamal. Portugal vs Spain. The Biggest World Cup Knockout Clash Lands in Dallas on Monday.
articles.excerpt: The Iberian rivals meet at AT&T Stadium for only the third time in World Cup history. Spain are unbeaten in 34 matches. Ronaldo has four goals and has scored in six World Cups. DFW's 300,000-strong Indian American community has a front-row seat.
articles.image_caption: Cristiano Ronaldo during an international match for Portugal
articles.nri_angle: AT&T Stadium in Arlington sits in the heart of DFW's 300,000-strong Indian American community. This World Cup clash between Ronaldo and Yamal is the biggest sporting event in their backyard this summer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Are In. Pakistan Might Be Out. Cricket's Olympic Return Has Already Redrawn the Map.
articles.excerpt: The IOC has approved the qualification pathway for LA 2028 — continental representation over global rankings leaves cricket's heavyweights fighting for one wildcard spot.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of the Knight Riders Cricket Ground in Pomona, California, the venue for cricket at the 2028 Olympics
articles.nri_angle: Cricket at the 2028 LA Olympics means NRIs in Southern California can watch India play live — at a stadium built by an Indian-owned franchise, scheduled for Indian prime-time viewing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nagelsmann Is Out. Klopp Is In. Germany's World Cup Reckoning Just Produced Football's Biggest Coaching Move.
articles.excerpt: A three-hour meeting in Frankfurt sealed the end. The DFB is already in talks with Jürgen Klopp, who has signalled willingness to return to the dugout for his country.
articles.image_caption: Jürgen Klopp on the touchline during his time as Liverpool manager
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs in the US and UK followed Klopp at Liverpool and watched Paraguay knock out Germany on American soil — now the man who built Anfield's revival could reshape football's most decorated national team from a continent away.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sriram Balaji Is India's Last Man Standing at Wimbledon. The Chennai Doubles Specialist Is Making the Most of It.
articles.excerpt: After a breakthrough quarter-final at Roland Garros last month, India's top-ranked doubles player has carried that momentum to the All England Club with an assured first-round start alongside Brazilian partner Marcelo Demoliner.
articles.image_caption: Sriram Balaji during an ATP tour match
articles.nri_angle: With no Indian singles players at Wimbledon this year, NRIs in the UK and US can rally behind Balaji — the Chennai-born doubles specialist who has quietly become India's most consistent Grand Slam performer in 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Teams, Six Points, and the Tightest MLC Race American Cricket Has Ever Seen
articles.excerpt: MI New York's five-run win over Seattle has left five of six franchises level on points with the playoffs a fortnight away. For NRIs across America, the sport they grew up with has never felt closer.
articles.image_caption: Grand Prairie Stadium, one of MLC's home venues in the Dallas–Fort Worth area
articles.nri_angle: MLC matches are being played in cities with large Indian tech communities — Redmond, Grand Prairie, Pomona, Fairfax — putting competitive T20 cricket within driving distance of NRIs across America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sumit Nagal Ends a Two-Year Title Drought in Romania. India's No. 1 Says He Questioned Everything.
articles.excerpt: The 28-year-old from Haryana, who fell from world No. 68 to No. 297, beat France's Felix Balshaw in the Intaro Open final for his seventh Challenger title. He says the hardest battle was against himself.
articles.image_caption: Sumit Nagal at the 2022 French Open qualifying rounds
articles.nri_angle: Nagal trained in Toronto as a teenager and has built his career across continents — a journey that mirrors the Indian diaspora's own experience of striving far from home with limited institutional support.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Messi Has 19 World Cup Goals, a Record No One Else Has Held, and Maybe Two Weeks Left. Cape Verde Stand in His Way.
articles.excerpt: The 39-year-old is the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history. On Friday night in Miami, the smallest nation ever to play a knockout match will try to end his farewell tour.
articles.image_caption: Lionel Messi celebrating during Argentina's World Cup 2026 group stage campaign
articles.nri_angle: Miami's large Indian-American community has embraced Messi since his Inter Miami move; this knockout match at Hard Rock Stadium is a must-watch for NRIs across South Florida and beyond.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Lost to Ireland. The Rain Stole Chester-le-Street. Old Trafford on Saturday Is Where Iyer's Team Has to Start Answering.
articles.excerpt: Varun Chakaravarthy's return, Sooryavanshi's wait, and a hostile England side await India in the second T20I at Manchester.
articles.image_caption: Old Trafford Cricket Ground in Manchester, the venue for the second India-England T20I
articles.nri_angle: Manchester's massive Indian and Pakistani community turns Old Trafford into a festival atmosphere when India tour; the Saturday afternoon slot makes it accessible for NRIs across the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oyarzabal Scores Twice. Spain Cruise Past Austria at SoFi and Haven't Conceded a Goal All Tournament.
articles.excerpt: La Roja's 3-0 demolition in Los Angeles — their fourth clean sheet in four matches — sets up an Iberian showdown with Portugal in Arlington on Monday.
articles.image_caption: Pedro Porro heads home Spain's second goal against Austria at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs across Southern California, Spain's dominant display at SoFi was a first-hand taste of World Cup football at its surgical best — and the Iberian showdown with Portugal heads to Arlington, TX, another diaspora hub.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: England Have Never Won a T20 World Cup at Home. Australia Have Never Lost a Final. Something Breaks at Lord's on Sunday.
articles.excerpt: The Women's T20 World Cup final between hosts England and six-time champions Australia at Lord's is the biggest match in the tournament's history — and Indian fans have their own reasons to keep watching.
articles.image_caption: Nat Sciver-Brunt batting for England in a Women's T20 World Cup match
articles.nri_angle: India's group-stage exit and the historic first women's Test at Lord's starting July 10 give NRI cricket fans in the UK two reasons to follow the final closely — and a reason to stay for the week after.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan's Knight Riders Just Became the First Cricket Franchise in the World to Own a Stadium
articles.excerpt: The Knight Riders Cricket Ground at Fairplex in Pomona opens with an MLC match, a Bollywood-sized dream, and a straight line to the 2028 Olympics.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of the Knight Riders Cricket Ground at Fairplex in Pomona, California

sources.label: Shah Rukh Khan on X (formerly Twitter)

articles.nri_angle: First franchise-owned cricket stadium in the US sits in Southern California's diaspora heartland, with 2028 Olympics significance for NRI cricket fans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ronaldo Scores His First World Cup Knockout Goal. Then Ramos Wins It in Stoppage Time. Portugal Edge Croatia in Toronto.
articles.excerpt: Cristiano Ronaldo equalised from the penalty spot, Gonçalo Ramos headed a 90th-minute winner, and a VAR-disallowed Croatian equaliser completed the chaos at BMO Field. Spain await in the round of 16.
articles.image_caption: Cristiano Ronaldo scored his first World Cup knockout-round goal in Portugal's dramatic 2-1 win over Croatia
articles.nri_angle: The match was played in Toronto, home to over 700,000 South Asians, with Spain vs Portugal next in Arlington, Texas — another major NRI hub.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: She Walked Back From Injury. She Walked England Into a World Cup Final. Nat Sciver-Brunt's 75 Was the Innings of the Tournament.
articles.excerpt: England captain returns from a calf strain, rescues her side from 23 for 3, and fires them into a Lord's final against Australia with a 133-run stand alongside Heather Knight.
articles.image_caption: Nat Sciver-Brunt batting for England in international cricket
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the UK have had front-row seats to a record-breaking Women's T20 World Cup, with the Lord's final and a historic women's Test against India both days away.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ashwin and Dravid Reunite in Dublin. Europe's First ICC-Sanctioned T20 League Just Got Its Star Power.
articles.excerpt: The European T20 Premier League held its inaugural draft on Thursday, with Ashwin captaining Dravid's franchise and Maxwell, Steve Waugh and Jonty Rhodes all owning teams across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands.
articles.image_caption: Ravichandran Ashwin during an international match for India
articles.nri_angle: The ETPL brings franchise cricket to Dublin, Belfast, Edinburgh and Glasgow — cities with large Indian and South Asian diaspora populations — letting NRIs in the UK and Europe watch Ashwin and Maxwell play on their doorstep.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Play Their First Test Series in Sri Lanka Since 2017. Here's What's at Stake.
articles.excerpt: Two World Test Championship matches at Galle and Colombo in August mark India's return to the island after an eight-year gap — with their WTC final hopes hanging in the balance.
articles.image_caption: Shubman Gill, India's Test captain, will lead the side in Sri Lanka
articles.nri_angle: Galle is one of the easiest and most popular overseas cricket destinations for Indian fans, and the first Test falls on India's Independence Day — making it a potential travel pilgrimage for NRIs across Asia and the Middle East.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
